chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy - Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas
chapters.summary: In this chapter: panchayati raj: local government in rural india; the gram panchayat and gram sabha; exemplary sarpanchs; child-friendly panchayats and children's parliament.

lessons.title: Panchayati Raj: Local Government in Rural India

activities.prompt: How can a village council make everyday life better for its people?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Visit to a Village Council
activities.body:
You begin your lesson in a village in India. This lesson focuses on local government in rural areas. You notice how large and diverse our country is. India has about 600,000 villages, 8,000 towns and over 4,000 cities. Almost two-thirds of India's population lives in rural areas.

As you walk around, you meet a Panchayat, which is a village council. It brings government closer to the people. Local people can take an active part in making decisions. You watch them discuss what their area needs.

As you continue your visit, you learn that Panchayati Raj is a form of self-government. The system has three levels. Its work includes agriculture, housing, roads and water resources. You see how it helps solve local problems and promote development.

Before you leave, you see Panchayats helping local development happen. Their work stays close to local needs. You understand that local government works through people and their choices. Your tour shows a village council as a centre of self-government.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Local government in rural India
activities.body: India is very big. It has many kinds of people and places. About two-thirds of India's people live in rural areas. A Panchayat is a village council (a group that makes village decisions). Panchayati Raj means self-government. Local people run it. It brings government closer to villages. Local people can join decisions. They can solve local problems. They can help development (making life better) grow. The system has three levels. Its work includes agriculture (farming), housing, roads and water resources (water for people).
keyPoints: A Panchayat is a village council.
Panchayati Raj is self-government by local people.
It has three levels. It covers local development work.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you understand local government in rural India.

activities.prompt: A village road is broken. Can villagers help choose its repair?
steps: A Panchayat is a village council, close to village life.
It can discuss roads because roads are part of its work.
It supports self-government because local people help make decisions.
Therefore, they can help choose how to repair the road.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Meaning of Panchayati Raj
activities.prompt: What does Panchayati Raj mean?
options: It is central government far from villages.
It is a form of self-government.
It is a list of India's towns.
It is a way to build houses alone.
activities.explanation: Panchayati Raj is a form of self-government, so local people govern their areas.

activities.title: Government close to people
activities.prompt: Panchayats bring government closer to the people.
activities.explanation: Yes, Panchayats bring government closer to rural communities.

activities.title: Complete the definition
activities.prompt: A Panchayat is a ______ council.
activities.hint: This council serves a small local area.
activities.explanation: A Panchayat is a village council.

activities.title: Match the ideas
activities.prompt: Match each Panchayati Raj idea with its correct meaning.
activities.explanation: Panchayats solve local problems and bring government closer through self-government.

activities.title: Why Panchayats matter
activities.prompt: Why do Panchayats matter in rural areas?
options: They change villages into towns and cities.
They bring government closer and help local development.
They move all government work out of villages.
They work only in the biggest cities.
activities.explanation: Panchayats bring government closer. They solve local problems and help villages develop.

activities.title: India and its local government
activities.prompt: Match each fact about India with its correct detail.
pairs: agriculture, housing, roads and water resources
activities.explanation: These details show India's scale and the Panchayati Raj system's work.

activities.prompt: Most Indians live in rural areas. Why are village councils useful?
options: They bring decisions close to most people's daily lives.
They replace the need for any central office.
They matter only when villages become towns.
They solve national problems instead of local ones.

why.They replace the need for any central of: This mistakes local help for a replacement of all higher services.
why.They matter only when villages become to: This wrongly thinks councils stop working when places grow.
why.They solve national problems instead of: This confuses local problems with national ones.

activities.explanation: This is right because local government is close to rural people.

activities.prompt: A village needs help with a road. Where should action begin?
options: At the Panchayat, because it handles local roads.
At a distant office, because distance makes choices fairer.
At each home, because a council cannot discuss roads.
At a town hall, because villages have no local council.

why.At a distant office, because distance ma: This wrongly treats distance as a reason for fairer decisions.
why.At each home, because a council cannot d: This wrongly believes only separate homes can discuss a road.
why.At a town hall, because villages have no: This wrongly assumes villages lack a local council.

activities.explanation: This is right because a Panchayat handles local roads.

activities.prompt: A map shows many villages across India. What can we conclude?
options: India has a large number of rural settlements.
India has one shared council for every village.
Most Indian villages have more people than cities.
Every Indian village uses the same roads and water.

why.India has one shared council for every v: This mistakes many settlements for one shared council.
why.Most Indian villages have more people th: This wrongly compares population without any population evidence.
why.Every Indian village uses the same roads: This wrongly assumes every village has identical local work.

activities.explanation: This is right because India has about 600,000 villages.

activities.prompt: Residents need better water. How can they use Panchayati Raj?
options: Join local meetings and help make decisions.
Wait quietly because only councils may make choices.
Make separate plans because shared decisions do not help.
Leave every choice to one distant office.

why.Wait quietly because only councils may m: This wrongly thinks participation means staying silent.
why.Make separate plans because shared decis: This wrongly believes separate plans work better than shared ones.
why.Leave every choice to one distant office: This wrongly gives all decisions to people far from the village.

activities.explanation: This is right because local people can take an active part.

activities.prompt: Why might villagers attend a Panchayat meeting about roads?
options: They can help decide because roads are part of local work.
They must attend because local decisions never affect daily life.
They attend to avoid learning how their village works.
They prefer distant offices because those repair roads faster.

why.They must attend because local decisions: This wrongly says local decisions have no effect on daily life.
why.They attend to avoid learning how their: This gives a negative reason instead of the real one.
why.They prefer distant offices because thos: This wrongly assumes distance makes road work faster.

activities.explanation: This is right because local people decide and roads are local work.

activities.prompt: A local plan includes housing, roads, and water. What does this show?
options: The plan fits work included in Panchayati Raj.
The plan only fits work done by large cities.
The plan is outside local government because it has several needs.
The plan proves Panchayati Raj has only one level.

why.The plan only fits work done by large ci: This wrongly treats city work as the only kind of work.
why.The plan is outside local government bec: This wrongly thinks several needs place a plan outside government.
why.The plan proves Panchayati Raj has only: This confuses one activity with the system's three levels.

activities.explanation: These are included in its work, so the plan fits.

lessons.title: The Gram Panchayat and Gram Sabha

activities.prompt: How do villagers choose the people who guide their village?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet Your Village Leaders
activities.body:
Imagine you live in a village and want decisions to begin very near your home. But what if you could help choose the people who manage village work?

Welcome to the Gram Panchayat, the level closest to rural people. Here, you learn that Gram Panchayat members are chosen directly by the Gram Sabha. The Gram Sabha consists of village adults who are enrolled as voters.

You watch as women and men in the Gram Sabha discuss matters concerning their area. After choosing the members, the Gram Panchayat elects a head called the Sarpanch or Pradhan. In recent years, more women have become Sarpanchs.

You also meet a Panchayat Secretary, who helps the Gram Panchayat with administrative work. The Secretary calls meetings and keeps records.

Many Gram Panchayats also receive help from an officer called the Patwari. The Patwari keeps records of villagers' land. Sometimes, the Patwari also keeps maps that are many generations old. During your visit, you see how village adults shape local leadership.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Village Jobs
activities.body: The Gram Panchayat is the level closest to village people. The Gram Sabha chooses its members. The Gram Sabha is all village adults who are registered voters. Women and men discuss issues in their area. The Gram Panchayat chooses a head. The head is called the Sarpanch or Pradhan. The Panchayat Secretary helps with office work. The Panchayat Secretary calls meetings and keeps records. A Patwari keeps land records and old maps for villagers.
keyPoints: The Gram Panchayat is closest to village people.
The Gram Sabha chooses members and talks about local issues.
The Secretary and Patwari keep records.
activities.explanation: These are the main jobs you will learn about in this lesson.

activities.prompt: A Panchayat meeting has ended. Who should keep its notes?
steps: The Panchayat Secretary calls meetings, so the Secretary handles them.
The Secretary also keeps records, so meeting notes fit this role.
The Patwari keeps land records, which serve a different need.
Therefore, the Panchayat Secretary should keep the meeting notes.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: The Gram Sabha has village adults who are voters.
activities.explanation: The Gram Sabha is made of village adults who are voters.

activities.prompt: Which level is closest to rural people?

The Gram Sabha

activities.prompt: A Panchayat needs meeting and land records. Who keeps each kind?
options: The Secretary keeps meeting records; the Patwari keeps land records.
The Patwari keeps meeting records; the Secretary keeps land records.
The Secretary and Patwari both keep only meeting records.
The Secretary and Patwari both keep only land records.

why.The Patwari keeps meeting records; the S: This swaps the two helpers’ work.

options: The elected Gram Panchayat members.
The enrolled adults in the Gram Sabha.
The Panchayat Secretary.
The village Patwari.

This confuses the adults’ choice with the members’ choice.

lessons.title: Exemplary Sarpanchs

activities.prompt: How can one village leader inspire an entire community?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Village Leaders at Work
activities.body:
You meet Dnyaneshwar Kamble in Tarangfal village. He became its Sarpanch through a tough election. He won against six other candidates. His motto was “lok seva, gram seva.” It means that serving the village is serving the public. You see how his guiding idea placed village service first.

Next, you enter a village led by Vandana Bahadur Maida. She challenged patriarchal norms and became its first female Sarpanch. She persuaded village women to attend Sabha meetings. She tackled education and sanitation, important issues for everyone.

Then you travel to Hiware Bazar, once troubled by frequent droughts and poor harvests. Its Sarpanch used a model of rainwater harvesting and watershed conservation. He also planted lakhs of trees. Within a few years, the village became green and prosperous.

Before you leave, you remember Popatrao Pawar. He received the Padma Shri award in 2020. The journey connects village service, women’s leadership, and environmental care.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Sarpanchs who served their villages
activities.body: Dnyaneshwar Kamble became Tarangfal village’s Sarpanch. His motto, lok seva, gram seva, meant serving the village is serving the public. Vandana Bahadur Maida challenged patriarchal norms, ideas favouring men. She became her village’s first female Sarpanch. She brought women into Sabha meetings and handled education and sanitation. Hiware Bazar’s Sarpanch saved rainwater and planted lakhs of trees. The village became green and prosperous within a few years.
keyPoints: Kamble’s motto linked village service with public service.
Maida became her village’s first female Sarpanch.
Water work and tree planting helped Hiware Bazar prosper.
activities.explanation: These Sarpanchs served villages and tackled important local problems.

activities.prompt: A village is choosing a Sarpanch. Why might people choose Kamble?
steps: Kamble's motto was lok seva, gram seva.
This means that serving the village is also serving the public.
He won against six other candidates, so the village selected him.
Therefore, people could see their choice as a choice of public service.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Who became the Sarpanch of Tarangfal village?
options: Vandana Bahadur Maida
Dnyaneshwar Kamble
Popatrao Pawar
activities.explanation: Kamble became the Sarpanch of Tarangfal village.

activities.prompt: Kamble’s motto meant that serving the village was serving the public.
activities.explanation: His motto directly connects village service with public service.

activities.prompt: Kamble won against ______ other candidates.
activities.hint: the lesson gives this number.
activities.explanation: Kamble won against six other candidates.

activities.prompt: Which Sarpanch persuaded village women to attend Sabha meetings?
options: Dnyaneshwar Kamble
Popatrao Pawar
Vandana Bahadur Maida
activities.explanation: Maida persuaded village women to attend Sabha meetings.

activities.prompt: Match each person, place, or problem with its matching fact.
activities.explanation: Each pair connects a person, place, or problem with a matching fact.

activities.prompt: Put Maida’s actions in the correct order.
items: became her village’s first female Sarpanch
persuaded village women to attend Sabha meetings
activities.explanation: The order moves from Maida’s challenge to her work as Sarpanch.

activities.prompt: Which actions helped Hiware Bazar become green and rich in a few years?
options: Saving rainwater and planting lakhs of trees
Holding Sabha meetings and not saving water
Buying water and having poor crops
Stopping tree planting and ignoring the water plan
activities.explanation: His water plan and lakhs of planted trees helped the village become green and rich.

activities.prompt: Who got the Padma Shri award in 2020?
options: Dnyaneshwar Kamble
Vandana Bahadur Maida
Popatrao Pawar
The Sarpanch of Hiware Bazar
activities.explanation: Popatrao Pawar got the Padma Shri award in 2020.

activities.prompt: A village has frequent droughts and poor harvests. Its Sarpanch uses rainwater harvesting and watershed conservation. What change is most likely?
options: The village became green and prosperous within a few years.
The village stayed poor because the new methods did not work.
The village grew more trees but stayed poor for many years.
The village needed less water because farming had completely stopped.

why.The village stayed poor because the new: This mistake thinks the water-saving methods had no effect.
why.The village grew more trees but stayed p: This mistake wrongly separates tree growth from the village's prosperity.
why.The village needed less water because fa: This mistake assumes farming stopped without any stated reason.

activities.explanation: This is right because this approach helped Hiware Bazar become green and prosperous.

activities.prompt: A map shows green areas across Hiware Bazar today. The village once suffered frequent droughts and poor harvests. What does the map help us understand?
options: The Sarpanch's water and tree work helped change the village.
The village had many trees before the Sarpanch began his work.
The map proves every year after that had no drought.
The village became green without using the water methods.

why.The village had many trees before the Sa: This wrongly places the trees before the Sarpanch's work.
why.The map proves every year after that had: A map cannot show that every later year had no drought.
why.The village became green without using t: This mistakes the green result for having no proper cause.

activities.explanation: This is right because the map and facts show change after this work.

lessons.title: Child-Friendly Panchayats and Children's Parliament

activities.prompt: How can children help shape the places where they live and learn?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Children Lead the Way
activities.body:
Imagine joining children's groups where young people speak up for themselves and their communities. You see Bal Panchayats working together to protect children's rights.

Some Bal Panchayats have worked to end child labour and child marriage. You watch members work together to persuade parents and other adults.

They also persuade adults not to arrange marriages for girls who should be studying. Their efforts have brought many children back to school. You see education become a shared goal.

Now you visit Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat. It gives great importance to children's needs and rights. The Panchayat built compound walls around schools to make them safer for children. It also built school kitchens so that students receive hygienically cooked mid-day meals.

Next, you enter the Children's Parliament, which grew from Bunker Roy's Barefoot College initiative. Underprivileged children were empowered through education and democratic participation. Children aged 8 to 14 join governance processes. They learn about democracy and social responsibility through night schools and elections. You see campaigning and voter ID cards, which show formal procedures in action.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: How These Groups Help Children
activities.body: Bal Panchayats work together for children. They persuade adults to end child labour and child marriage. This means stopping marriages for girls who should be studying. They bring many children back to school. Gram Panchayats can build safer schools and school kitchens. Democratic participation means taking part in decisions.
keyPoints: Bal Panchayats support children's schooling and rights.
Some Gram Panchayats build safer schools and kitchens.
The Children's Parliament includes children in democratic participation.
activities.explanation: These groups help children learn, stay safe and take part.

activities.prompt: A girl is studying, but adults plan to marry her soon. What can a Bal Panchayat do to protect her schooling?
steps: Members should work together, because Bal Panchayats persuade parents and adults as a group.
They should persuade adults against the marriage, because she should keep studying.
Their effort can end child marriage and keep the girl in school.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What do Bal Panchayat members do together?
options: Build school kitchens
Persuade parents and other adults
Give voter ID cards
Lead night schools
activities.explanation: Bal Panchayat members work together to persuade parents and other adults. Good work can change children's lives.

activities.prompt: The Gram Panchayat built ______ around schools to make them safer.
activities.hint: These walls surround the school.
activities.explanation: It built compound walls around schools. These walls made schools safer for children.

activities.prompt: Match each part with its matching fact.
pairs: Learning about democracy and social responsibility
activities.explanation: Each pair shows a special action or feature. Together, they support children's learning and safety.

activities.prompt: Which option best describes the different roles of these groups?
options: Bal Panchayats lead elections. The Parliament builds compound walls.
Bal Panchayats cook mid-day meals. The Parliament ends child labour.
Bal Panchayats support children's schooling. The Parliament teaches and includes children in governance.
Bal Panchayats use voter ID cards. The Parliament persuades parents.
activities.explanation: Bal Panchayats support children's schooling through persuasion and local actions. The Parliament provides education and democratic participation.

activities.prompt: Some adults want to marry girls who should study. A Bal Panchayat speaks with them together. What may happen?
options: Adults may stop planning marriages because the community speaks together.
Adults will marry girls sooner because children keep talking to them.
Girls will stop studying because adults agree to their marriages.
Adults will keep their plan because children cannot change decisions.

why.Adults will marry girls sooner because c: This mistake thinks pressure from children helps, rather than protects girls.
why.Girls will stop studying because adults: This mistake reverses the result, because studying should continue, not stop.
why.Adults will keep their plan because chil: This mistake thinks children have no influence over adult decisions.

activities.explanation: Speaking together can persuade adults, so girls may continue studying.

activities.prompt: Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat built school walls and kitchens. What do these actions show?
options: The Panchayat gives importance to children's safety, meals, and needs.
The Panchayat wants children to leave school because kitchens make meals.
The Panchayat thinks safety matters less than food for children.
The Panchayat wants adults alone to decide children's school needs.

why.The Panchayat wants children to leave sc: This mistake thinks kitchens were built to keep children away from school.
why.The Panchayat thinks safety matters less: This mistake treats safety and meals as opposites, although both matter.
why.The Panchayat wants adults alone to deci: This mistake thinks adults must decide, although children's needs are central.

activities.explanation: Compound walls protect children, and kitchens provide hygienically cooked meals.

activities.prompt: An 8-year-old and a 14-year-old join a Children's Parliament meeting. What should the meeting allow?
options: Both children should take part in the governance process.
Only the 8-year-old should take part because children must be young.
Only the 14-year-old should take part because older children know more.
Neither child should take part because adults must make every decision.

why.Only the 8-year-old should take part bec: This mistake treats young age as the only rule, ignoring children up to 14.
why.Only the 14-year-old should take part be: This mistake thinks age removes the right to participate before fourteen.
why.Neither child should take part because a: This mistake assumes adults have all participation rights and children have none.

activities.explanation: Children aged 8 to 14 take part, so both children should participate.

activities.prompt: A source shows a Children's Parliament election, campaigns, and voter ID cards. What does it show?
options: The Parliament uses formal ways to organize children's democratic participation.
The Parliament avoids elections because children cannot make choices.
The Parliament uses campaigns to stop children from taking part.
The Parliament treats voting as a game without any real rules.

why.The Parliament avoids elections because: This mistake thinks elections are avoided, although the source shows one.
why.The Parliament uses campaigns to stop ch: This mistake reverses the purpose of campaigns, which support participation.
why.The Parliament treats voting as a game w: This mistake sees formal rules as pretend, although the procedures are real.

activities.explanation: Elections, campaigns, and voter ID cards are formal procedures in the Parliament.

activities.prompt: The Children's Parliament educated underprivileged children and included them in democratic participation. Why was this useful?
options: It helped underprivileged children learn and take part in democracy.
It stopped underprivileged children from learning and making choices.
It gave children power but did not teach social responsibility.
It helped children attend school but removed their democratic voice.

why.It stopped underprivileged children from: This mistake thinks empowerment means excluding children from learning and decisions.
why.It gave children power but did not teach: This mistake separates power from responsibility, although children learn both.
why.It helped children attend school but rem: This mistake says participation was removed, although democratic participation was central.

activities.explanation: Education and participation together empowered underprivileged children.

activities.prompt: A Bal Panchayat persuades adults, while a Children's Parliament lets children vote. What do both methods do?
options: Both help children influence decisions about their lives.
Both stop children from taking any part in community decisions.
Both make adults avoid thinking about children's needs.
Both replace children's actions with actions taken only by adults.

why.Both stop children from taking any part: This mistake thinks influence means exclusion, although both methods involve children.
why.Both make adults avoid thinking about ch: This mistake reverses the result, because adult decisions still include children's needs.
why.Both replace children's actions with act: This mistake thinks only adults act, although children act in both places.

activities.explanation: Persuading adults and voting both let children shape decisions.

lessons.title: Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad

activities.prompt: What happens when Gram Panchayats share their development plans?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: From Gram Panchayat to Zila Parishad
activities.body:
Imagine visiting village institutions during a short tour. You begin at the Gram Panchayat, where local people elect members. Its members may also include village Sarpanchs and local State Assembly members.

Now meet the Panchayat Samiti. It coordinates matters across Gram Panchayats. It collects development plans from all the Gram Panchayats. Next, it combines these plans and presents them at district or State levels. This helps provide funds for development projects.

You travel to the Zila Parishad. The Panchayat Samiti connects the Gram Panchayat with it.

Here, one-third of seats are reserved for women at all three levels. Special rules help disadvantaged sections make their needs heard.

Finally, remember that Panchayat Samiti composition differs from State to State. Their role in strengthening local participation remains the same. The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana promotes all-weather rural roads.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Local groups work together
activities.body: Panchayat Samitis help local people take part in development. Their members differ between States. But their role stays the same. They collect plans from all Gram Panchayats. Then they combine the plans. They present these plans at district or State level. This helps get money for development projects. The Panchayat Samiti links the Gram Panchayat with the Zila Parishad. Special rules help disadvantaged groups make their needs heard.
keyPoints: Their role in helping local people take part stays the same.
Plans are combined and shown at district or State level.
One-third of seats are kept for women at all three levels.
activities.explanation: Great start! These groups turn local plans into action for development.

activities.prompt: Two Gram Panchayats have different development plans. How can the Panchayat Samiti help them move forward together?
steps: The Samiti collects plans from all Gram Panchayats, so every plan is included.
It combines these plans, so the villages can be considered together.
It presents them at district or State levels, so the combined plans can move upward.
This helps provide funds for development projects, giving the villages development support.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What happens after Panchayat Samitis combine Gram Panchayat plans?
options: Collect development plans
Reserve one-third of their seats
Promote all-weather rural roads
Present them at district or State levels
activities.explanation: After combining the plans, Panchayat Samitis present them at district or State levels.

activities.prompt: The Panchayat Samiti links the Gram Panchayat to which group?
options: Zila Parishad
State Assembly
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
Disadvantaged sections
activities.explanation: The Panchayat Samiti links the Gram Panchayat with the Zila Parishad.

activities.prompt: Panchayat Samitis collect ______ plans from all Gram Panchayats.
activities.hint: These plans from all Gram Panchayats are combined.
activities.explanation: Panchayat Samitis collect development plans from all Gram Panchayats.

activities.prompt: Match each item with the correct fact.
pairs: One-third of seats are reserved at all three levels
Help disadvantaged sections make their needs heard
Village Sarpanchs and local State Assembly members
Connects the Gram Panchayat with the Zila Parishad
activities.explanation: Each pair shows a role or rule described in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Put the Panchayat Samiti's steps in order.
items: Collect plans from all Gram Panchayats
Present them at district or State levels
Help provide funds for development projects
activities.explanation: Plans move from collection to combining, presentation, and funding support.

activities.prompt: What do local people do with these institutions?
options: They collect development plans
They combine the plans
They connect the Gram Panchayat with the Zila Parishad
They elect their members
activities.explanation: Local people elect members of these institutions.

activities.prompt: Both Gram Panchayats send development plans to their Panchayat Samiti. What should the Samiti do next?
options: Combine the plans and present them at district or State level.
Hold a new election for every Gram Panchayat member.
Reserve one-third of the seats for women first.
Ask the Zila Parishad to choose the Samiti members.

why.Hold a new election for every Gram Panch: This confuses a planning step with choosing representatives.
why.Reserve one-third of the seats for women: Reserved seats are about representation, not combining plans.
why.Ask the Zila Parishad to choose the Sami: Local people elect the members, not the Zila Parishad.

activities.explanation: This is the next step after the Samiti collects the plans.

activities.prompt: A map shows links among the three local-government levels. Which path is correct?
options: Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti → Zila Parishad.
Gram Panchayat → Zila Parishad → Panchayat Samiti.
Panchayat Samiti → Gram Panchayat → State Assembly.
Zila Parishad → Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti.

why.Gram Panchayat → Zila Parishad → Panchay: This reverses the correct order of the connection.
why.Panchayat Samiti → Gram Panchayat → Stat: The Assembly may be included, but it is not the middle link.
why.Zila Parishad → Gram Panchayat → Panchay: This reverses the order and puts the Samiti last.

activities.explanation: This is the connection between the three local-government levels.

activities.prompt: Plans from several Gram Panchayats are combined and presented at a higher level. What may follow?
options: Funds may be provided for development projects.
Local elections may be held in every village next.
Women may receive one-third of all seats then.
Members may change the Samiti's composition next.

why.Local elections may be held in every vil: This confuses the funding result with choosing representatives.
why.Women may receive one-third of all seats: This confuses representation rules with development funding.
why.Members may change the Samiti's composit: This confuses a possible funding result with changing membership.

activities.explanation: Presenting combined plans can help provide funds for development projects.

lessons.title: Local Self-Government and Old Ideas of Administration

activities.prompt: How do villages govern (rule) themselves? What can we learn from the past?
activities.explanation: Read on to find out.

activities.title: A Tour of Local Self-Government
activities.body:
As you begin your visit, you meet the Panchayati Raj institutions. You notice that their functions differ a little among States. You soon understand why. States have authority over these institutions.

Their main aim is to enable villagers to take an active part. You watch this participation include developing their villages and local area. You see villagers acting for the places where they live.

Now you turn towards an ancient text about governance. It is called the Arthaśhāstra. Kauṭilya wrote it about 2,300 years ago. Its four categories guide your tour.

First, you see a sangrahaṇa for every 10 villages. Next comes a kārvaṭika for every 100 villages. Then you find a droṇamukha for every 400 villages. Finally, you meet a sthānīya for every 800 villages.

Finally, you return to Panchayati Raj democracy. You see both direct participation and elected representatives. Together, these forms support villagers’ active part.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Local Participation and Village Administration
activities.body: Panchayati Raj lets villagers take part. It includes developing villages and local areas. Its work is a little different in each State. States have authority over it. The Arthaśhāstra is an old text about governance. Kauṭilya wrote it about 2,300 years ago. Sangrahaṇa, kārvaṭika, droṇamukha and sthānīya were four types of village administration. Panchayati Raj is a democracy. It uses direct participation and elected representatives.
keyPoints: Villagers take part in local development.
States have authority over Panchayati Raj institutions.
The Arthaśhāstra lists four types of village administration.
activities.explanation: These ideas link local participation, State authority and old administration.

activities.prompt: Why can local functions differ among States while villagers still share the same main aim?
steps: Because States have authority, their functions can differ a little.
Their shared aim is to enable villagers to take an active part.
That active part includes developing their village and local area.
So different functions do not remove the shared participation aim.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Why are the functions of Panchayati Raj a little different in each State?
options: Every State must have exactly the same functions.
States have authority over these bodies.
Old texts decide each State's functions.
Only elected leaders can work with Panchayati Raj.
activities.explanation: States have authority (power to decide) over Panchayati Raj bodies. This power explains the differences.

activities.prompt: Panchayati Raj has one main aim. The aim is to help villagers take an active part.
activities.explanation: Correct. Villagers can take an active part in local work.

activities.prompt: Kauṭilya wrote the Arthaśhāstra about ______ years ago.
activities.hint: This number tells how long ago he wrote it.
activities.explanation: Kauṭilya wrote the Arthaśhāstra about 2,300 years ago.

activities.prompt: Match each administration category to its number of villages.
activities.explanation: Each category served a different number of villages, from 10 to 800.

activities.prompt: Which administration category served every 400 villages?
options: sangrahaṇa
kārvaṭika
droṇamukha
sthānīya
activities.explanation: Droṇamukha was the third category. It served every 400 villages.

activities.prompt: In Panchayati Raj democracy, people take part only directly.
activities.explanation: It uses both direct participation and elected representatives.

activities.prompt: Put the categories in order, from fewest villages to most.
activities.explanation: The categories go from 10 villages for sangrahaṇa up to 800 villages for sthānīya.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is true about villagers and the State?
options: Villagers build local areas. But the State has no power over them.
The State stops villagers from taking part in local work.
The State controls all local work. Villagers do nothing.
Villagers build local areas. The State has power over Panchayati Raj groups.
activities.explanation: Villagers take part in local work. The State still has power over these groups.

activities.prompt: State A changes how local institutions work. What may happen in State B?
options: Its functions may differ a little from State A.
Its functions must become exactly the same.
It will lose all authority over local institutions.
Villagers there cannot take an active part.

why.Its functions must become exactly the sa: This wrongly assumes authority makes State functions identical.
why.It will lose all authority over local in: This wrongly assumes States lose their authority.
why.Villagers there cannot take an active pa: This wrongly assumes State authority removes village participation.

activities.explanation: Different State authority allows local functions to differ a little.

activities.prompt: Villagers discuss a need, then choose representatives. What does this show?
options: It joins direct participation with elected representatives.
It uses only direct discussion by villagers.
It uses only people chosen through an election.
It keeps villagers separate from local decisions.

why.It uses only direct discussion by villag: This wrongly leaves out elected representatives.
why.It uses only people chosen through an el: This wrongly leaves out direct participation.
why.It keeps villagers separate from local d: This wrongly treats elected representatives as separate from villagers.

activities.context: India is a large and diverse country, and almost two-thirds of its people live in rural areas. In a rural village, residents face problems with roads and water resources. activities.prompt: If the Panchayat is addressing the village's water-resource problem, what is the best way to handle it?
options: Let residents help choose how the village's water resources should be managed.
Let people outside the village decide alone, keeping decisions away from local residents.
Choose a plan without asking residents, since their participation is unnecessary.
Leave the issue to distant authorities, because the village council cannot help solve local problems.

why.Let people outside the village decide al: Panchayats bring government closer to people.
why.Choose a plan without asking residents,: Residents can take an active part in making decisions.
why.Leave the issue to distant authorities,: Panchayats help to solve local problems.

activities.explanation: This uses local participation and active decision-making.

The Panchayat would cease to be a village council because it handled only one subject.

Residents would lose all say because the Panchayat had made one decision.

why.The Panchayat would still solve every lo: The work of a Panchayat includes more than roads.
why.The Panchayat would cease to be a villag: A Panchayat remains a village council regardless of the subjects considered.
why.Residents would lose all say because the: Local participation does not disappear because one subject is considered.

activities.explanation: Water resources are included in the Panchayati Raj system's work.

activities.prompt: Explain why Panchayati Raj is useful for solving problems in rural areas.
activities.answer: Panchayati Raj is a form of self-government with three levels. It brings government closer to people in rural areas. points: Panchayati Raj is self-government.

activities.context: In a village, adults who were enrolled as voters gathered as the Gram Sabha. activities.prompt: Suppose more village adults become enrolled as voters. Who can then directly choose the Gram Panchayat members?
options: The newly enrolled adults, because they become Gram Sabha members and directly select the Panchayat members.
Only adults selected as Gram Panchayat members, because choosing the members makes them Gram Sabha members.
Only the Sarpanch or Pradhan, because the elected head alone represents the Gram Sabha.
Only village adults not enrolled as voters, because taking part does not require voter enrollment.

why.Only adults selected as Gram Panchayat m: These adults directly choose Gram Panchayat members.
why.Only the Sarpanch or Pradhan, because th: Being chosen as a Panchayat member does not make someone a Gram Sabha member.
why.Only village adults not enrolled as vote: The elected head is not the only person in the Gram Sabha.

activities.explanation: The Gram Sabha includes village adults enrolled as voters.

activities.context: In a village, adults who were enrolled as voters gathered as the Gram Sabha. Women and men discussed matters concerning their area and directly chose the Gram Panchayat members, who then elected a woman as Sarpanch. A Panchayat Secretary called the meeting and kept the records. A Patwari who helped the Gram Panchayat kept records of villagers' land and sometimes kept maps that were many generations old. activities.prompt: A member finds a map that is many generations old while reviewing village information. Who should the member ask about this map and the villagers' land records?

The Panchayat Secretary, because this officer keeps every kind of village record.
The Sarpanch or Pradhan, because the elected head personally maintains all land records.
The Gram Sabha members, because they are selected to check land records.

why.The Panchayat Secretary, because this of: The Patwari sometimes keeps maps that are many generations old.
why.The Sarpanch or Pradhan, because the ele: The Secretary's duties concern meetings and records for the Panchayat.
why.The Gram Sabha members, because they are: There is no fact that the elected head keeps land records.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between the Gram Sabha and the Gram Panchayat?
activities.answer: The Gram Sabha consists of village adults who are enrolled as voters. It discusses matters concerning the area and directly chooses Gram Panchayat members. points: The Gram Sabha consists of village adults enrolled as voters.
It discusses matters concerning the area.
It directly chooses Gram Panchayat members.
The Gram Panchayat elects the Sarpanch or Pradhan.

activities.context: Dnyaneshwar Kamble became Sarpanch of Tarangfal after beating six candidates. His motto, lok seva, gram seva, meant serving the village serves the public. Vandana Bahadur Maida became her village’s first female Sarpanch, challenged patriarchal norms, persuaded women to attend Sabha meetings, and addressed education and sanitation. Hiware Bazar’s Sarpanch faced droughts and poor harvests, used rainwater harvesting and watershed conservation, and planted lakhs of trees. It became green and prosperous within a few years. Popatrao Pawar received Padma Shri in 2020.
activities.prompt: If Tarangfal faces a choice affecting the whole village, what should Kamble do according to his motto?
options: Consider how the choice will benefit the village as a whole.
Give priority to one group’s wishes even if they harm the village.
Ignore village needs and follow personal convenience.
Leave the decision to others without considering the village’s needs.

why.Give priority to one group’s wishes even: This favours one group instead of the whole village.
why.Ignore village needs and follow personal: This places personal comfort above serving others.
why.Leave the decision to others without con: This avoids considering how the decision serves the village.

activities.explanation: This follows the idea that village service is public service.

activities.context: Dnyaneshwar Kamble became Sarpanch of Tarangfal after beating six candidates. His motto, lok seva, gram seva, meant serving the village serves the public. Vandana Bahadur Maida became her village’s first female Sarpanch, challenged patriarchal norms, persuaded women to attend Sabha meetings, and addressed education and sanitation. activities.prompt: If another drought occurs in Hiware Bazar, what should its Sarpanch continue doing to support the village?

Stop all tree planting because trees are no longer needed.
Use only a single water-collection effort and abandon conservation work.
Wait for better harvests without preparing for drought.

why.Stop all tree planting because trees are: Ending tree planting would remove an important part of the successful approach.
why.Use only a single water-collection effor: A single effort would not continue the complete conservation approach.
why.Wait for better harvests without prepari: Waiting without preparing would fail to address recurring drought conditions.

activities.explanation: Rainwater harvesting, watershed conservation and tree planting helped the village prosper.

activities.prompt: How did Maida’s leadership change who took part and what issues received attention?
activities.answer: Maida challenged patriarchal norms by becoming her village’s first female Sarpanch. She persuaded village women to attend Sabha meetings, bringing them into village decision-making. She also dealt with important issues such as education and sanitation. Her leadership therefore combined women’s participation with attention to important village needs.
points: She became her village’s first female Sarpanch.
She challenged patriarchal norms.
She persuaded women to attend Sabha meetings.
She dealt with education and sanitation.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Children in Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat needed safer schools and hygienically cooked mid-day meals. The panchayat built compound walls and school kitchens for these purposes. Elsewhere, the Children’s Parliament, which grew from Bunker Roy’s Barefoot College initiative, empowered underprivileged children through education and democratic participation. Children aged 8 to 14 take part in governance, learn about democracy and social responsibility, and use formal procedures such as voter ID cards.
activities.prompt: If the compound walls around the schools had not been built, what would most likely have happened?
options: The schools would not have become as safe for children.
The students would have received less hygienically cooked meals.
The children would have lost the chance to take part in elections.
The Parliament would have stopped using voter ID cards.

why.The students would have received less hy: The school kitchens were a separate measure for mid-day meals.
why.The children would have lost the chance: The Parliament’s elections were connected to children’s democratic participation.
why.The Parliament would have stopped using: Voter ID cards were used in the Parliament, not around the schools.

Avoid campaigning because elections should be quiet.

why.Avoid campaigning because elections shou: Campaigning is part of the children’s democratic participation.

why.Let adults campaign so the children do n: Children aged 8 to 14 take part in governance themselves.

activities.context: Residents have elected members of the Gram Panchayat and Panchayat Samiti. The combined plan will be withdrawn because it has reached the district level.
Local participation will end because the plans have left the villages.
The Panchayat Samiti will no longer need to collect plans from Gram Panchayats.

why.The combined plan will be withdrawn beca: Presentation is meant to seek support, not withdraw the plan.
why.Local participation will end because the: Preparing the joint plan continues the process of strengthening local participation.
why.The Panchayat Samiti will no longer need: The Samiti continues coordinating matters and collecting Gram Panchayat plans.

activities.context: Residents have elected members of the Gram Panchayat and Panchayat Samiti. why.The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana wou: Removing them would not directly affect the road scheme.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between the composition and the role of Panchayat Samitis.
activities.answer: The composition of Panchayat Samitis differs from State to State, so the way they are made up can vary. Their participation helps develop villages and local areas, through direct involvement and elected representatives.

chapters.summary: In this chapter: how democracy works in cities; urban local bodies and wards; functions of urban local bodies; the history of municipal corporations.

lessons.title: How Democracy Works in Cities

activities.prompt: How can your voice shape the city you live in?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Tour of City Governance
activities.body:
Imagine you are touring a city and wondering who helps make decisions there. In a democracy, good governance aims to empower citizens so they can take part. You can take part at rural, regional, urban, state and national levels.

This sharing of power in decision-making is called participatory democracy. As you explore, you learn that power in decision-making can be shared. Urban areas are generally more complex and diverse than rural areas.

That complexity means urban governance needs to be more complex as well. This lesson focuses on the basic principles of urban governance. You also see how participatory democracy works in an urban area.

Now picture the governance pyramid. The Union Government is at the top. Earlier, you explored the rural side of the pyramid. This time, you move to its urban side. You see how power is shared across levels.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Participatory Democracy in Urban Areas
activities.body: Good governance in a democracy aims to empower citizens so they can take part. Citizens can take part at rural, regional, urban, state and national levels. Sharing power in decision-making is called participatory democracy. This lesson looks at its basic principles in urban areas. Urban areas are generally more complex and diverse than rural areas. The Union Government is at the top of the governance pyramid.
keyPoints: Good governance empowers citizens.
Sharing power in decision-making is participatory democracy.
Urban governance needs to be more complex.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you understand how citizens share power in urban governance.

activities.prompt: A city has many different groups. How should its people help make decisions?
steps: The city is urban, so it is usually complex and diverse.
Urban governance must be complex because it must handle urban complexity.
Good governance should empower citizens so they can take part.
When citizens share decisions, this is participatory democracy.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Aim of Good Governance
activities.prompt: What does good governance aim to do in a democracy?
options: Empower citizens so they can take part.
Keep all decisions private.
Stop citizens from taking part.
activities.explanation: Good governance aims to empower citizens so they can take part.

activities.title: Sharing Power
activities.prompt: Sharing power in decision-making is called ______ democracy.
activities.hint: This word describes citizens sharing power in decisions.
activities.explanation: Sharing power in decision-making is called participatory democracy.

activities.title: Ideas and Meanings
activities.prompt: Match each idea with its meaning.
activities.explanation: Good governance empowers citizens, while participatory democracy shares decision-making power.

activities.title: How Participation Works
activities.prompt: Put these steps in the best order.
items: Good governance aims to empower citizens.
Citizens can take part in governance.
This sharing is called participatory democracy.
activities.explanation: Empowerment helps citizens take part, and sharing power is participatory democracy.

activities.title: The Chapter's Focus
activities.prompt: Which statement best matches this chapter's focus?
options: The basic principles of urban governance.
The basic principles of rural governance.
Only the powers of the Union Government.
activities.explanation: This chapter focuses on urban governance and how participatory democracy works in urban areas.

activities.prompt: A resident speaks in city and state meetings. What does this show?
options: Citizens can take part at urban and state levels.
They can take part only at the city level.
They cannot take part at two levels.
They need power only at the pyramid top.

why.They can take part only at the city leve: The first wrongly limits participation to urban governance.
The second wrongly says citizens cannot take part twice.
The third wrongly puts citizen power only at the top.

One person keeps all decision power.
Only residents keep all decision power.
Only local leaders keep all decision power.

This wrongly shows one person holding all decision-making power.
This wrongly leaves local leaders without any shared power.
why.Only local leaders keep all decision pow: This wrongly leaves residents without any shared power.

activities.prompt: An urban area is diverse. How should its governance be organised?

It should stay simple and ignore urban needs.
It should focus on only one kind of group.

why.It should stay simple and ignore urban n: This wrongly ignores the greater complexity of urban areas.
why.It should focus on only one kind of grou: This wrongly ignores the different groups found in urban areas.
why.It should keep citizens out of city deci: This wrongly removes citizens from urban governance.

activities.explanation: Urban governance must be more complex because urban areas are complex.

lessons.title: Urban Local Bodies and Wards

activities.prompt: How could your neighbourhood have a say in local decisions?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Your Tour of Urban Local Bodies
activities.body:
Imagine walking through your city or town. You see local government structures nearby. These are called urban local bodies.

They are decentralised. Local communities have a direct say in how their areas are managed.

Each city and town is divided into smaller areas called wards. During your walk, you enter one of these areas. A ward committee organises activities here.

Committee members organise useful activities, such as health camps. They can also campaign against the use of single-use plastics. Their work helps communities deal with the issues they face.

As you continue your tour, the committee watches for problems. These may include leaking water, blocked drains or damaged roads. It reports these problems to the authorities. Finally, remember that the way wards function differs from State to State.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: How urban local bodies work
activities.body: Urban local bodies are local governments in cities and towns. They are decentralised. This means decisions are made near local people. Local people have a direct say. They help run their areas. Cities and towns are divided into smaller areas. These areas are called wards. Ward committees plan activities. They watch for problems. They report problems to the authorities. The way wards work is different in each State.
keyPoints: Urban local bodies are decentralised local governments.
Local people have a direct say in running their areas.
Wards are small areas inside cities and towns.
Ward committees plan activities and report problems to authorities.
activities.explanation: This card explains wards and how problems are reported.

activities.prompt: Water is leaking near homes. What can residents do, and why?
steps: Water leaking near homes matters because it is a local problem.
Residents can raise it with the ward committee because it helps communities deal with issues.
The committee can report it to authorities because reporting local problems is its role.
This shows decentralised management because communities have a direct say in their area.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What are urban local bodies?
options: Local government groups in cities and towns
Groups that only work against plastic
Big areas that split cities into states
Offices that report problems outside towns
activities.explanation: Urban local bodies are local government groups in cities and towns.

activities.prompt: Cities and towns are divided into smaller areas called ______.
activities.hint: They are smaller parts of cities and towns.
activities.explanation: These smaller areas are called wards.

activities.prompt: Match each group or place with its role.
pairs: Have a direct say in managing their areas
Organise activities such as health camps
Smaller areas within cities and towns
activities.explanation: Local communities have a say, while ward committees organise and report.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order.
items: Ward committees report problems to authorities
activities.explanation: Town areas contain wards, whose committees organise work and report problems.

activities.prompt: Which problem should a ward committee watch for?
options: A health camp
A blocked drain
A campaign against single-use plastics
A difference between States
activities.explanation: Blocked drains are among the problems ward committees watch for.

activities.prompt: A ward committee finds a broken road. What should it do next?
options: Hold a health camp
Fight against single-use plastic
Report it to the officials
Split the town into states
activities.explanation: A ward committee watches for broken roads. It reports them to officials.

activities.prompt: Water is leaking near homes. What should the ward committee do?
options: Watch for the leak, then report it to the authorities.
Wait for the leak to disappear without taking action.
Report only after the road becomes damaged.
Keep the leak inside the committee without telling anyone.

why.Wait for the leak to disappear without t: This mistake thinks problems will fix themselves without action.
why.Report only after the road becomes damag: This mistake limits reporting to damaged roads.
why.Keep the leak inside the committee witho: This mistake thinks local problems should stay hidden.

activities.explanation: This is right because committees watch for and report local problems.

activities.prompt: A shop uses lots of single-use plastic bottles. Which action best fits the committee's role?
options: Campaign against the use of single-use plastics.
Organise a health camp instead of plastic action.
Watch for leaking water and damaged roads.
Ask the authorities to create more wards.

why.Organise a health camp instead of plasti: This mistake mixes up plastic campaigning with health camps.
why.Watch for leaking water and damaged road: This mistake focuses on physical problems instead of plastic use.
why.Ask the authorities to create more wards: This mistake treats ward creation as the answer to plastic use.

activities.explanation: This is right because committees can campaign against single-use plastics.

activities.prompt: In State A, ward committees report problems. In State B, they work differently. What can we conclude?
options: Ward work can differ from State to State.
Every State must use exactly the same method.
Only State A has local government bodies.
Problems must be handled in the same way everywhere.

why.Every State must use exactly the same me: This mistake assumes all States follow one identical method.
why.Only State A has local government bodies: This mistake treats one State's example as the rule for all.
why.Problems must be handled in the same way: This mistake assumes every place handles problems in the same way.

activities.explanation: This is right because ward work can change between States.

activities.prompt: Residents want a health camp in their ward. Which action best shows local management?
options: Residents help decide on a health camp for their area.
Only distant officials should decide about the camp.
People from another city should choose the camp.
The ward committee should ignore residents' wishes.

why.Only distant officials should decide abo: This mistake gives all local choices to distant officials.
why.People from another city should choose t: This mistake moves local decisions to people from another city.
why.The ward committee should ignore residen: This mistake ignores the community's direct say.

activities.explanation: This is right because local communities have a direct say in management.

activities.prompt: A map shows a town split into many small areas. What can the map tell us?

why.The map shows where water leaks are foun: This mistake treats a boundary map as a problems map.
why.The map shows only one central governmen: This mistake thinks the town has no smaller local areas.

lessons.title: Functions of Urban Local Bodies

activities.prompt: What makes our neighbourhood work, and how can you help?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Tour of Local Services
activities.body:
Imagine beginning a tour of your neighbourhood with an urban local body. It quietly performs many functions that help daily life. You may notice paths, pipes, and other local infrastructure. The body helps look after these shared facilities. So it keeps the area working smoothly.

Now, your tour enters a burial ground. Local bodies maintain burial grounds. They also collect and dispose of garbage. At waste collection points, they make disposal easier for everyone. Separating waste correctly helps this work. Following waste-segregation instructions does the same.

Next, you see government schemes being checked. They also collect local taxes and fines. The body also helps plan the area’s economic and social development. Your visit shows how many services meet local needs.

Finally, you discover that citizens have important duties. Performing these duties helps local bodies work efficiently. You must show care and concern for your area. Report a leaking water pipe promptly to prevent wasting precious water. With your help, the local body can serve everyone better.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: How urban local bodies help your area
activities.body: Urban local bodies look after infrastructure. Infrastructure means the basic facilities in your area. They look after burial grounds. They collect and get rid of garbage. They check government schemes. They collect local taxes and fines. They help plan economic and social development. This means how an area grows and improves. Citizens must do their duties. Citizens must show care and concern. Citizens separate waste correctly and follow the rules. They report leaking water pipes quickly.
keyPoints: Urban local bodies have many functions.
They look after infrastructure and help plan development.
Citizens must do their duties and care for their area.
activities.explanation: These jobs help local services work better for everyone.

activities.prompt: A water pipe starts leaking near homes in the neighborhood.
steps: Residents notice the leak and report it promptly because this can prevent wasting precious water.
They show care and concern for their area by taking this step.
Citizens perform their duties so that local bodies can work efficiently.
Reporting the leak helps protect a precious resource.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which is a function of urban local bodies?
options: They look after local infrastructure.
They collect school fees.
They make new laws for the country.
They sell food in markets.
activities.explanation: Urban local bodies help look after local infrastructure.

activities.prompt: Urban local bodies help plan their area’s economic and social development.
activities.explanation: Planning development is one of their important functions.

activities.prompt: Urban local bodies collect and dispose of ______.
activities.hint: This is waste from homes and businesses.
activities.explanation: Collecting and disposing of garbage keeps local services working properly.

activities.prompt: Match each urban local body function with its work.
activities.explanation: Each activity helps urban local bodies serve their local area.

activities.prompt: Put these urban local body functions in the order given.
activities.explanation: These functions cover many parts of local life.

activities.prompt: Why should you report a leaking water pipe promptly?
options: To help prevent the waste of precious water.
To make the pipe become longer.
To collect a local fine.
To check a government scheme.
activities.explanation: Reporting a leak promptly can prevent precious water from being wasted.

activities.prompt: Separating waste correctly makes garbage collection easier.
activities.explanation: Correct separation helps garbage collection work more easily.

activities.prompt: A citizen cares about the area. Which citizen duty is this?
options: Doing jobs that help local bodies work well.
Taking all garbage to a graveyard.
Collecting local taxes and fines.
Checking government plans.
activities.explanation: Citizens must do their duties. They must care about their area.

activities.prompt: In a neighborhood, people put wet and dry waste together. What may happen?
options: Garbage collection can become harder.
Garbage collection can become much easier.
The area can need less local care.
The local body can stop collecting garbage.

why.Garbage collection can become much easie: This is wrong because separating waste makes collection easier.
This mistake ignores that local bodies look after local needs.
why.The local body can stop collecting garba: This mistake thinks garbage disposal is not a local-body function.

activities.explanation: Mixing waste makes correct separation harder, so collection can become harder.

activities.prompt: Area A follows waste-segregation instructions, but Area B mixes waste. Which is likely?
options: Area A's garbage collection is easier.
Area B's garbage collection is easier.
Both areas need no garbage collection.
Area A must stop caring for its area.

This is wrong because mixing waste does not make collection easier.
This mistake ignores the work local bodies do with garbage.
This mistake turns helpful citizen action into neglect.

activities.explanation: Following waste-segregation instructions makes garbage collection easier.

lessons.title: The History of Municipal Corporations

activities.prompt: How did cities begin caring for their own communities?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Tour of City Government
activities.body:
You begin your tour at Fort St. George. The East India Company issued a charter. The charter included the fort and nearby territories. It was issued one year before the corporation was established.

The corporation began on 29 September 1688. Today, you know it as the Greater Chennai Corporation. It is the oldest municipal institution in India. This journey shows how a charter could start a city corporation.

In 1792, an Act of Parliament gave the Madras Corporation power to collect municipal taxes. Proper municipal administration began when the city gained this power. You now see why tax power marked proper municipal administration.

Your tour continues to Bombay. The Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai was first called the Bombay Municipal Corporation. It was created in 1865. Together, these stories show how municipal corporations developed in India. You have travelled through the history of city government.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: From Charter to Corporation
activities.body: The Madras Corporation is now called the Greater Chennai Corporation. It was started on 29 September 1688. It is the oldest municipal body in India. One year earlier, the East India Company gave it a charter. The charter covered Fort St. George and nearby land. In 1792, Parliament passed an Act. The Act let it collect municipal taxes. Real municipal government began then.
keyPoints: The Madras Corporation was started on 29 September 1688.
The East India Company gave the charter.
The 1792 Act let the corporation collect municipal taxes.
activities.explanation: These facts show how the corporation grew, from its charter to real municipal government.

activities.prompt: A city has a charter, but its leaders cannot collect municipal taxes. How can proper municipal administration begin?
steps: A charter created the corporation, because it gave the city its start.
The Act of Parliament in 1792 gave tax power, because it allowed municipal taxes.
Municipal administration properly began then, because gaining tax power marked its proper start.
Therefore, the city needed municipal tax power before proper administration could begin.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Corporation's New Name
activities.prompt: What is the Madras Corporation called now?
options: Madras Corporation
Greater Chennai Corporation
Bombay Municipal Corporation
Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai
activities.explanation: The Madras Corporation is now called the Greater Chennai Corporation.

activities.title: Year It Started
activities.prompt: The Madras Corporation started on 29 September ______.
activities.hint: Think of the year it started.
activities.explanation: The corporation started on 29 September 1688.

activities.title: Places in the Charter

options: Fort St. George only
Fort St. George and nearby territories
Bombay and nearby territories
Greater Mumbai only

activities.title: Match the Correct Partners

activities.title: Why Did Municipal Administration Begin?
activities.prompt: Why does the lesson say that municipal administration properly began in 1792?
options: The East India Company issued the charter.
The Madras Corporation changed its name.
The Bombay Municipal Corporation was created.
The city gained power to levy municipal taxes.
activities.explanation: The city gained power to levy municipal taxes. Proper municipal administration began then.

activities.prompt: The Madras corporation began in 1688. Bombay's began in 1865. Which city began earlier?
options: Madras began in 1688, before Bombay began in 1865.
Bombay began in 1865, before Madras began in 1688.
Both cities began in the same year.
Madras began after Bombay because of renaming.

why.Bombay began in 1865, before Madras bega: This reverses the two starting years.
This wrongly treats different years as the same year.
why.Madras began after Bombay because of ren: This confuses renaming with the earlier start of the corporation.

activities.explanation: This is right because 1688 is earlier than 1865.

options: Gain power to levy municipal taxes.
Rename the city corporation.
Move Fort St George away.
Make a new city charter.

Making another charter is not the change linked to proper administration.

activities.explanation: This is right because proper administration began with municipal tax power.

options: Charter, corporation, tax power.
Corporation, charter, tax power.
Tax power, charter, corporation.
Charter, tax power, corporation.

This reverses the charter and the corporation.
This puts 1792 before events that happened earlier.
This places tax power before the corporation was established.

activities.explanation: This is right because the charter came before the 1688 corporation.

lessons.title: Types of Urban Local Bodies and Their Services

activities.prompt: A city needs help with water, waste, or certificates. What happens then?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Tour of Urban Local Bodies
activities.body:
You begin your tour in Chennai or Indore. A Municipal Corporation is at the top of its urban bodies. Only cities with a population above 10 lakhs have this highest body. A Municipal Corporation is also called a Mahanagar Nigam.

Now, you visit a city with a population between 1 and 10 lakhs. Its highest urban body is a Municipal Council. A Municipal Council is also called a Nagar Palika. In smaller cities and towns, you find a Nagar Panchayat.

At Indore Municipal Corporation, you see business, hoardings and trade licences handled. Its listed services include property tax, water charges and solid waste management. The chapter's service list is simplified.

Next, you explore citizen services. Marriage certificates, fire services and various licences are included. Water tankers and debris clearance are citizen services too. Citizen Relationship Management is shortened to CRM.

As your tour ends, you remember three urban body types. Municipal Corporations are highest in cities above 10 lakhs. Municipal Councils are highest in cities with 1 to 10 lakhs. Smaller cities and towns have Nagar Panchayats.
activities.explanation: Reading first helps the ideas stick.

activities.title: Urban local bodies
activities.body: Cities have different local bodies. Cities above 10 lakhs have a Municipal Corporation. It is called a Mahanagar Nigam. Cities with 1 to 10 lakhs have a Municipal Council. It is called a Nagar Palika. Small towns and cities have a Nagar Panchayat. Indore Municipal Corporation gives services. These include property tax, water charges and solid waste management. Citizen services include certificates, fire services and licences. It also gives water tankers and debris clearance.
keyPoints: Municipal Corporations serve cities above 10 lakhs.
Municipal Councils serve cities with 1 to 10 lakhs.
Nagar Panchayats serve smaller cities and towns.
activities.explanation: This card tells about each big local body. It also tells about some Indore services.

activities.prompt: Eight lakh people live in a city. The city wants to know which urban body should be highest.

Nagar Panchayat
Municipal Corporation

activities.prompt: One to ten lakhs fits the Municipal Council rule. A city has eight lakhs. Which body is highest?
options: The city has a Municipal Council because eight lakhs fits its range.
The city has a Municipal Corporation because every large city gets one.

why.The city has a Municipal Corporation bec: This mistake thinks any large city can have a Municipal Corporation.
why.The city has a Nagar Panchayat because i: This mistake uses the rule for smaller populations instead of the council range.
why.The city has a Municipal Corporation bec: This mistake reverses the population limit for a Municipal Corporation.

activities.prompt: City A has twelve lakhs. City B has eight lakhs. Which comparison is correct?
options: City A has a Municipal Corporation; City B has a Municipal Council.
City A has a Municipal Council; City B has a Municipal Corporation.

why.City A has a Nagar Panchayat; City B has: This mistake treats twelve lakhs as a smaller-population place.
why.Both cities have Municipal Corporations: This mistake assumes all large cities have Municipal Corporations.

activities.explanation: This is right because twelve lakhs is above ten and eight is within the range.

activities.prompt: Indore Municipal Corporation handles business, hoardings and trade licences. Does this prove every Municipal Corporation does the same?
options: No. The fact tells us about Indore Municipal Corporation only.
Yes. Every Municipal Corporation handles these same three matters.
Yes. Every Municipal Council handles these same three matters.
Yes. Chennai Municipal Corporation must handle these same three matters.

why.Yes. Every Municipal Corporation handles: This mistake turns one city's service list into a rule for every corporation.
why.Yes. Every Municipal Council handles the: This mistake gives corporation work to Municipal Councils.
why.Yes. Chennai Municipal Corporation must: This mistake assumes Chennai has the same services as Indore.

options: The list gives some services, not the full service list.

The list gives only citizen services and omits all other services.

why.The list gives every service in complete: This mistake treats a simplified list as a complete list.
why.The list gives no services because it is: This mistake thinks simplified means empty.
why.The list gives only citizen services and: This mistake confuses a simplified list with a list of one service group.
